result:
The experiment design is written to `runs/pending_experiment.json`.

**Design summary:** Since the champion's exact pretrained trunk is banned this round, I traced why every prior from-scratch/split-capacity attempt lost (25 straight reverted rounds): they were all *smaller* than champion's capacity, either because a from-scratch trunk cost 4 bytes/weight at float32 or because a dispatcher/specialist split fragmented the budget across two heads (exp-59's own capacity-vs-interference risk note was borne out — it lost catastrophically). The pivot: train every trunk/field/confidence weight with an 8-bit straight-through fake-quantization during training, then actually export via `onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic` to real int8 weights — turning the byte budget that has starved every prior from-scratch attempt into ~4x more room. That freed room goes into a genuinely wider depthwise-separable from-scratch trunk (320ch vs the old 48-190ch range) and a single unified field head at a finer 40×40 grid, with the exp-12 gate/dark-expert split deleted outright.

Every non-frozen stage (trunk, rotation-fan wiring, field, decode, confidence, plus new training-signal and export stages) is marked `changed: true` with a concrete, real code diff specified in the implementation brief — no torchvision import, no checkpoint file, nothing that would trip `backbonecheck.py`.
